title: Superconducting landscape of the strongly correlated bilayer Hubbard model
authors: Motoharu Kitatani, Yusuke Nomura, Shiro Sakai, Ryotaro Arita
abstract: Coupling two strongly correlated layers opens a distinct route to repulsion-driven superconductivity. Yet the same interlayer coupling makes the optimization of superconductivity highly nontrivial. Using the dynamical vertex approximation, we determine the superconducting landscape in the enlarged parameter space spanned by filling and interlayer hopping. We identify an optimal regime at intermediate interlayer hopping and moderate doping away from half filling, where the system exhibits high superconducting transition temperatures ($T_{\rm c}$) with an interband $s_{\pm}$-wave gap structure. Toward half filling, however, strong self-energy effects can suppress the superconducting tendency by reducing the low-energy spectral weight. We further show that a Fermi-surface distortion induced by longer-range hoppings can weaken this suppression and enhance $T_{\rm c}$. Our results establish how filling, interlayer hopping, and Fermi-surface geometry jointly optimize the superconducting regime in the strongly correlated bilayer Hubbard model.
summary: This work maps the superconducting phase diagram of the bilayer Hubbard model, showing that optimal superconductivity occurs at intermediate interlayer coupling and doping. The authors demonstrate that strong correlations suppress $T_c$ near half-filling by reducing low-energy spectral weight, suggesting that modifying the Fermi surface geometry via longer-range hopping can enhance pairing.
main_problem: The study investigates how repulsive interactions drive superconductivity in a coupled, strongly correlated bilayer Hubbard model, and how external parameters control this superconducting state.
main_result: Superconductivity is optimized at intermediate interlayer hopping and moderate doping, exhibiting an $s_{\pm}$-wave gap; however, strong self-energy effects suppress $T_c$ near half-filling.
method: The research employs advanced theoretical techniques, primarily the Dynamical Vertex Approximation (D$\Gamma$A) and comparison with the Fluctuation Exchange (FLEX) approximation, to solve the linearized gap equation.
model_or_system: The system is the strongly correlated bilayer Hubbard model on a square lattice, described by a Hamiltonian including onsite repulsion ($U$) and interlayer hopping ($t_\perp$). The physics is analyzed by treating layer degrees of freedom via pseudo momentum $k_z$.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), superconducting eigenvalue ($\lambda_{SC}$), low-energy spectral weight, and the real/imaginary parts of the self-energy ($\Sigma$).
important_parameters: Filling ($n$), interlayer hopping ($t_\perp$), and interaction strength ($U/t$). Optimal regimes are found at intermediate $t_\perp$ and moderate doping.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations like D$\Gamma$A and FLEX, which are used to capture strong correlations and nonlocal fluctuations. A key assumption is that the superconducting pairing is governed by the interplay between these correlation effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the superconducting phase diagram ($T_c$ vs. filling), momentum-space maps showing spectral weight suppression near half-filling, and comparisons of $\lambda_{SC}$ across different theoretical approximations and temperature regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the superconducting landscape by first establishing the optimal doping/hopping regime, then detailing the mechanism of $T_c$ suppression near half-filling due to self-energy effects, and finally proposing that longer-range hoppings can mitigate this suppression.
why_interesting: The detailed study of how correlation-induced spectral weight suppression limits $T_c$ provides a rich theoretical framework relevant to understanding pairing mechanisms in high-temperature superconductors, which is a core area of condensed matter theory.
